contracts.boundary: Auto allowance recovery requires proof of the first user message for the current agent activity. A second user message, including consumed steering, makes recovery ineligible until agent_settled; missing lifecycle proof fails closed. Legacy Auto degradation for a new user request is permitted only when the last dispatched model remains a candidate in the selected or fallback pool.
contracts.assertions: Real Pi sessions in reliability v1 and v2 execute a synthetic tool, consume queued steering and receive an empty allowance failure without dispatching an alternate; a later independent settled turn still recovers once. Scratch-only removal of the new guard turns the named assertion red in each mode and restores green. Existing queued follow-up dispatch and empty Pi retry controls also pass. A registered-event harness emits the Pi lifecycle and verifies absent lifecycle proof fails closed in both versions. Real Pi sessions confirm a model removed from the selected/fallback pools is not dispatched after reload in both reliability versions; an unrelated tier, empty pool, and configured-but-unhealthy fallback are covered.

boundaryTest.name: does not retry a queued steering message after tool activity in v1

invariant.name: does not retry a queued steering message after tool activity in v2

fault.name: proves consumed steering activity blocks replay in v1

contracts.boundary: After a final failed turn, Pi-style 429 text is an explicitly labeled inference, not HTTP status evidence. It causes a bounded five-second provider pause; structured non-429 status remains authoritative during normalization.
contracts.assertions: Real Pi tests exercise actual HTTP 429 and an HTTP 200 stream lookalike in v1 Auto and physical mode and v2 Auto. Both trigger the visibly inferred pause and a subsequent turn avoids the same provider. An unrelated 500 and a successful native retry do not trigger the pause. The lookalike is an accepted, bounded false-positive tradeoff. No retry or Retry-After propagation is inferred.

boundaryTest.name: temporarily avoids a provider for inferred 429 (1, rate-limit-429, auto)

invariant.name: keeps ambiguous Pi-formatted 429 text as a heuristic

fault.exception: Before the implementation, the real Pi boundary test failed because the inferred 429 did not create a provider pause; after the change it passes. The prior no-pause assertion for the HTTP 200 lookalike was intentionally replaced by an explicit bounded-false-positive control.
